sources.entry: Benchmarking the Evolution of Performance and Energy Efficiency Across Recent Generations - Bandwidth-bound codes on Sapphire, Emerald and Granite Rapids and Sierra Forest with clocks, SMT and compiler stated.

summary.title: Benchmarking the Evolution of Performance and Energy Efficiency Across Recent Generations of Intel Xeon Processors
summary.one_liner: Learn how Intel Xeon generations (Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids, Sierra Forest) compare in runtime and energy use on bandwidth-bound HPC workloads.
takeaways: Intel launched four Xeon families in about 1.5 years: Sapphire Rapids (with an on-package HBM version), Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids (performance-oriented) and Sierra Forest (efficiency-oriented).
The paper benchmarks CPUs from these generations and variants with a focus on bandwidth-bound HPC applications.
Runtime and energy consumption are contrasted, and trends across generations are tracked.
summary.summary: This IEEE workshop paper (SC24-W, 2024, by Drávai and Reguly) evaluates the performance and energy efficiency of Intel Xeon CPUs from Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids and Sierra Forest. The work centers on bandwidth-bound high performance computing applications. It compares runtime and energy consumption figures and tracks trends across the generations. The listing notes the tests cover clocks, SMT and compiler settings, but the abstract provided does not give specific results.
